title: Sheldrake's crystals growing faster after the first growth
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Sheldrake's crystals growing faster after the first growth, about unspecified at unspecified, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: stuff points you know you'll grow a crystal lattice structure in a petri dish and it takes a long time to grow the first time and then it grows much much faster after you've grown it that first time

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea from a biologist named Rupert Sheldrake: when you grow a new kind of crystal in a lab dish, it takes a long time the first time, then grows much faster after that. If true, it would suggest nature has a kind of memory, with things getting easier once they have happened somewhere before.
